chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Whoever says at the end of the obligatory prayer, 'O One who does what He wills and does not do what others will, there is none other than Him,' three times, then asks, he will be given what he asked for.

key_terms.يَا مَنْ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ: O One who does what He wills

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after the obligatory prayer to ensure one's requests are granted?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the efficacy of invoking Allah’s absolute sovereignty (Al-Mashi’ah) as a means to secure the fulfillment of needs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between divine will and human supplication. The phrase 'He does what He wills and does not do what He wills' underscores that while God’s power is unrestricted, He chooses to grant requests made with sincere faith, linking the supplicant’s desire directly to the Divine Decree. This practice is often cited by scholars to demonstrate the spiritual potency of specific dhikr formulas in closing the obligatory prayers.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘The one who says at the end of the Obligatory (Salāt), ‘O Oneazwj Who Does whatever Heazwj so Desires to and does not do what anyone else desires’, three times, then asks, would be Given what he asks for’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘ Ammar who has said the following: “
Whoever, after every obligatory prayer says: ‘O the One who does as He wills and does not do as others will,’ three times, and pleads (before Allah) for his wishes they will be granted.’”
